gene.name: actin alpha 2, smooth muscle
gene.function: Actins are highly conserved proteins that are involved in various types of cell motility and are ubiquitously expressed in all eukaryotic cells.

gene.name: angiogenic factor with G-patch and FHA domains 1
gene.function: Promotes angiogenesis and the proliferation of endothelial cells. Able to bind to endothelial cells and promote cell proliferation, suggesting that it may act in an autocrine fashion. .

gene.name: angiotensin II receptor type 1
gene.function: Receptor for angiotensin II, a vasoconstricting peptide, which acts as a key regulator of blood pressure and sodium retention by the kidney. The activated receptor in turn couples to G-alpha proteins G(q) (GNAQ, GNA11, GNA14 or GNA15) and thus activates phospholipase C and increases the cytosolic Ca(2+) concentrations, which in turn triggers cellular responses such as stimulation of protein kinase C.

gene.name: AKT serine/threonine kinase 1
gene.function: AKT1 is one of 3 closely related serine/threonine-protein kinases (AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3) called the AKT kinase, and which regulate many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis. This is mediated through serine and/or threonine phosphorylation of a range of downstream substrates. Over 100 substrate candidates have been reported so far, but for most of them, no isoform specificity has been reported. AKT is responsible of the regulation of glucose uptake by mediating insulin-induced translocation of the SLC2A4/GLUT4 glucose transporter to the cell surface (By similarity). Phosphorylation of PTPN1 at 'Ser-50' negatively modulates its phosphatase activity preventing dephosphorylation of the insulin receptor and the attenuation of insulin signaling (By similarity). Phosphorylation of TBC1D4 triggers the binding of this effector to inhibitory 14-3-3 proteins, which is required for insulin-stimulated glucose transport. AKT also regulates the storage of glucose in the form of glycogen by phosphorylating GSK3A at 'Ser-21' and GSK3B at 'Ser-9', resulting in inhibition of its kinase activity (By similarity). Phosphorylation of GSK3 isoforms by AKT is also thought to be one mechanism by which cell proliferation is driven (By similarity). AKT also regulates cell survival via the phosphorylation of MAP3K5 (apoptosis signal-related kinase). Phosphorylation of 'Ser-83' decreases MAP3K5 kinase activity stimulated by oxidative stress and thereby prevents apoptosis. AKT mediates insulin-stimulated protein synthesis by phosphorylating TSC2 at 'Ser-939' and 'Thr-1462', thereby activating the mTORC1 signaling pathway, and leading to both phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 and in activation of RPS6KB1. Also regulates the mTORC1 signaling pathway by catalyzing phosphorylation of CASTOR1 and DEPDC5. AKT plays a role as key modulator of the AKT-mTOR signaling pathway controlling the tempo of the process of newborn neurons integration during adult neurogenesis, including correct neuron positioning, dendritic development and synapse formation (By similarity). Part of a positive feedback loop of mTORC2 signaling by mediating phosphorylation of MAPKAP1/SIN1, promoting mTORC2 activation (By similarity). AKT is involved in the phosphorylation of members of the FOXO factors (Forkhead family of transcription factors), leading to binding of 14-3-3 proteins and cytoplasmic localization. In particular, FOXO1 is phosphorylated at 'Thr-24', 'Ser-256' and 'Ser-319'. FOXO3 and FOXO4 are phosphorylated on equivalent sites. AKT has an important role in the regulation of NF-kappa-B-dependent gene transcription and positively regulates the activity of CREB1 (cyclic AMP (cAMP)-response element binding protein). The phosphorylation of CREB1 induces the binding of accessory proteins that are necessary for the transcription of pro-survival genes such as BCL2 and MCL1. AKT phosphorylates 'Ser-454' on ATP citrate lyase (ACLY), thereby potentially regulating ACLY activity and fatty acid synthesis (By similarity). Activates the 3B isoform of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (PDE3B) via phosphorylation of 'Ser-273', resulting in reduced cyclic AMP levels and inhibition of lipolysis (By similarity). Phosphorylates PIKFYVE on 'Ser-318', which results in increased PI(3)P-5 activity (By similarity). The Rho GTPase-activating protein DLC1 is another substrate and its phosphorylation is implicated in the regulation cell proliferation and cell growth (By similarity). Signals downstream of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI(3)K) to mediate the effects of various growth factors such as platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), epidermal growth factor (EGF), insulin and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1). AKT mediates the antiapoptotic effects of IGF1 (By similarity). Essential for the SPATA13-mediated regulation of cell migration and adhesion assembly and disassembly. May be involved in the regulation of the placental development (By similarity). Phosphorylates STK4/MST1 at 'Thr-120' and 'Thr-387' leading to inhibition of its: kinase activity, nuclear translocation, autophosphorylation and ability to phosphorylate FOXO3. Phosphorylates STK3/MST2 at 'Thr-117' and 'Thr-384' leading to inhibition of its: cleavage, kinase activity, autophosphorylation at Thr-180, binding to RASSF1 and nuclear translocation. Phosphorylates SRPK2 and enhances its kinase activity towards SRSF2 and ACIN1 and promotes its nuclear translocation. Phosphorylates RAF1 at 'Ser-259' and negatively regulates its activity. Phosphorylation of BAD stimulates its pro-apoptotic activity. Phosphorylates KAT6A at 'Thr-369' and this phosphorylation inhibits the interaction of KAT6A with PML and negatively regulates its acetylation activity towards p53/TP53. Phosphorylates palladin (PALLD), modulating cytoskeletal organization and cell motility. Phosphorylates prohibitin (PHB), playing an important role in cell metabolism and proliferation. Phosphorylates CDKN1A, for which phosphorylation at 'Thr-145' induces its release from CDK2 and cytoplasmic relocalization. These recent findings indicate that the AKT1 isoform has a more specific role in cell motility and proliferation. Phosphorylates CLK2 thereby controlling cell survival to ionizing radiation. Phosphorylates PCK1 at 'Ser-90', reducing the binding affinity of PCK1 to oxaloacetate and changing PCK1 into an atypical protein kinase activity using GTP as donor. Also acts as an activator of TMEM175 potassium channel activity in response to growth factors: forms the lysoK(GF) complex together with TMEM175 and acts by promoting TMEM175 channel activation, independently of its protein kinase activity. Acts as a regulator of mitochondrial calcium uptake by mediating phosphorylation of MICU1 in the mitochondrial intermembrane space, impairing MICU1 maturation. Acts as an inhibitor of tRNA methylation by mediating phosphorylation of the N-terminus of METTL1, thereby inhibiting METTL1 methyltransferase activity. In response to LPAR1 receptor pathway activation, phosphorylates Rabin8/RAB3IP which alters its activity and phosphorylates WDR44 which induces WDR44 binding to Rab11, thereby switching Rab11 vesicular function from preciliary trafficking to endocytic recycling.

gene.name: AKT serine/threonine kinase 2
gene.function: Serine/threonine kinase closely related to AKT1 and AKT3. All 3 enzymes, AKT1, AKT2 and AKT3, are collectively known as AKT kinase. AKT regulates many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis, through the phosphorylation of a range of downstream substrates. Over 100 substrates have been reported so far, although for most of them, the precise AKT kinase catalyzing the reaction was not specified. AKT regulates glucose uptake by mediating insulin-induced translocation of the SLC2A4/GLUT4 glucose transporter to the cell surface. Phosphorylation of PTPN1 at 'Ser-50' negatively modulates its phosphatase activity preventing dephosphorylation of the insulin receptor and the attenuation of insulin signaling. Phosphorylation of TBC1D4 triggers the binding of this effector to inhibitory 14-3-3 proteins, which is required for insulin-stimulated glucose transport. AKT also regulates the storage of glucose in the form of glycogen by phosphorylating GSK3A at 'Ser-21' and GSK3B at 'Ser-9', resulting in inhibition of its kinase activity. Phosphorylation of GSK3 isoforms by AKT is also thought to be one mechanism by which cell proliferation is driven. AKT also regulates cell survival via the phosphorylation of MAP3K5 (apoptosis signal- related kinase). Phosphorylation of 'Ser-83' decreases MAP3K5 kinase activity stimulated by oxidative stress and thereby prevents apoptosis. AKT mediates insulin-stimulated protein synthesis by phosphorylating TSC2 at 'Ser-939' and 'Thr-1462', thereby activating mTORC1 signaling and leading to both phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 and in activation of RPS6KB1. AKT is involved in the phosphorylation of members of the FOXO factors (Forkhead family of transcription factors), leading to binding of 14-3-3 proteins and cytoplasmic localization. In particular, FOXO1 is phosphorylated at 'Thr-24', 'Ser-256' and 'Ser-319'. FOXO3 and FOXO4 are phosphorylated on equivalent sites. AKT has an important role in the regulation of NF-kappa-B-dependent gene transcription and positively regulates the activity of CREB1 (cyclic AMP (cAMP)-response element binding protein). The phosphorylation of CREB1 induces the binding of accessory proteins that are necessary for the transcription of pro-survival genes such as BCL2 and MCL1. AKT phosphorylates 'Ser- 454' on ATP citrate lyase (ACLY), thereby potentially regulating ACLY activity and fatty acid synthesis. Activates the 3B isoform of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase (PDE3B) via phosphorylation of 'Ser-273', resulting in reduced cyclic AMP levels and inhibition of lipolysis. Phosphorylates PIKFYVE on 'Ser-318', which results in increased PI(3)P- 5 activity. The Rho GTPase-activating protein DLC1 is another substrate and its phosphorylation is implicated in the regulation cell proliferation and cell growth. AKT plays a role as key modulator of the AKT-mTOR signaling pathway controlling the tempo of the process of newborn neurons integration during adult neurogenesis, including correct neuron positioning, dendritic development and synapse formation. Signals downstream of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI(3)K) to mediate the effects of various growth factors such as platelet- derived growth factor (PDGF), epidermal growth factor (EGF), insulin and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1). AKT mediates the antiapoptotic effects of IGF1. Essential for the SPATA13-mediated regulation of cell migration and adhesion assembly and disassembly. May be involved in the regulation of the placental development. In response to lysophosphatidic acid stimulation, inhibits the ciliogenesis cascade. In this context, phosphorylates WDR44, hence stabilizing its interaction with Rab11 and preventing the formation of the ciliogenic Rab11-FIP3-RAB3IP complex. Also phosphorylates RAB3IP/Rabin8, thus may affect RAB3IP guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) activity toward Rab8, which is important for cilia growth. Phosphorylates PKP1, facilitating its interaction with YWHAG and translocation to the nucleus, ultimately resulting in a reduction in keratinocyte intercellular adhesion (By similarity). Phosphorylation of PKP1 increases PKP1 protein stability, translocation to the cytoplasm away from desmosome plaques and PKP1- driven cap-dependent translation.

gene.name: arrestin beta 2
gene.function: Functions in regulating agonist-mediated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling by mediating both receptor desensitization and resensitization processes. During homologous desensitization, beta-arrestins bind to the GPCR-phosphorylated receptor and sterically preclude its coupling to the cognate G protein; the binding appears to require additional receptor determinants exposed only in the active receptor conformation. The beta-arrestins target many receptors for internalization by acting as endocytic adapters (CLASPs, clathrin-associated sorting proteins) and recruiting the GPRCs to the adapter protein 2 complex 2 (AP-2) in clathrin-coated pits (CCPs). However, the extent of beta-arrestin involvement appears to vary significantly depending on the receptor, agonist and cell type. Internalized arrestin-receptor complexes traffic to intracellular endosomes, where they remain uncoupled from G proteins. Two different modes of arrestin-mediated internalization occur. Class A receptors, like ADRB2, OPRM1, ENDRA, D1AR and ADRA1B dissociate from beta-arrestin at or near the plasma membrane and undergo rapid recycling. Class B receptors, like AVPR2, AGTR1, NTSR1, TRHR and TACR1 internalize as a complex with arrestin and traffic with it to endosomal vesicles, presumably as desensitized receptors, for extended periods of time. Receptor resensitization then requires that receptor-bound arrestin is removed so that the receptor can be dephosphorylated and returned to the plasma membrane. Mediates endocytosis of CCR7 following ligation of CCL19 but not CCL21. Involved in internalization of P2RY1, P2RY4, P2RY6 and P2RY11 and ATP-stimulated internalization of P2RY2. Involved in phosphorylation-dependent internalization of OPRD1 and subsequent recycling or degradation. Involved in ubiquitination of IGF1R. Beta- arrestins function as multivalent adapter proteins that can switch the GPCR from a G protein signaling mode that transmits short-lived signals from the plasma membrane via small molecule second messengers and ion channels to a beta-arrestin signaling mode that transmits a distinct set of signals that are initiated as the receptor internalizes and transits the intracellular compartment. Acts as a signaling scaffold for MAPK pathways such as MAPK1/3 (ERK1/2) and MAPK10 (JNK3). ERK1/2 and JNK3 activated by the beta-arrestin scaffold are largely excluded from the nucleus and confined to cytoplasmic locations such as endocytic vesicles, also called beta-arrestin signalosomes. Acts as a signaling scaffold for the AKT1 pathway. GPCRs for which the beta- arrestin-mediated signaling relies on both ARRB1 and ARRB2 (codependent regulation) include ADRB2, F2RL1 and PTH1R. For some GPCRs the beta- arrestin-mediated signaling relies on either ARRB1 or ARRB2 and is inhibited by the other respective beta-arrestin form (reciprocal regulation). Increases ERK1/2 signaling in AGTR1- and AVPR2-mediated activation (reciprocal regulation). Involved in CCR7-mediated ERK1/2 signaling involving ligand CCL19. Is involved in type-1A angiotensin II receptor/AGTR1-mediated ERK activity. Is involved in type-1A angiotensin II receptor/AGTR1-mediated MAPK10 activity. Is involved in dopamine-stimulated AKT1 activity in the striatum by disrupting the association of AKT1 with its negative regulator PP2A. Involved in AGTR1-mediated chemotaxis. Appears to function as signaling scaffold involved in regulation of MIP-1-beta-stimulated CCR5-dependent chemotaxis. Involved in attenuation of NF-kappa-B-dependent transcription in response to GPCR or cytokine stimulation by interacting with and stabilizing CHUK. Suppresses UV-induced NF-kappa- B-dependent activation by interacting with CHUK. The function is promoted by stimulation of ADRB2 and dephosphorylation of ARRB2. Involved in p53/TP53-mediated apoptosis by regulating MDM2 and reducing the MDM2-mediated degradation of p53/TP53. May serve as nuclear messenger for GPCRs. Upon stimulation of OR1D2, may be involved in regulation of gene expression during the early processes of fertilization. Also involved in regulation of receptors other than GPCRs. Involved in endocytosis of TGFBR2 and TGFBR3 and down-regulates TGF-beta signaling such as NF-kappa-B activation. Involved in endocytosis of low-density lipoprotein receptor/LDLR. Involved in both localization to primary cilium and endocytosis of smoothened (SMO) in a GRK2-dependent process. Involved in endocytosis of SLC9A5. Involved in endocytosis of ENG and subsequent TGF-beta-mediated ERK activation and migration of epithelial cells. Involved in Toll-like receptor and IL-1 receptor signaling through the interaction with TRAF6 which prevents TRAF6 autoubiquitination and oligomerization required for activation of NF-kappa-B and JUN. Involved in insulin resistance by acting as insulin-induced signaling scaffold for SRC, AKT1 and INSR. Involved in regulation of inhibitory signaling of natural killer cells by recruiting PTPN6 and PTPN11 to KIR2DL1. Involved in IL8-mediated granule release in neutrophils. Involved in the internalization of the atypical chemokine receptor ACKR3. Acts as an adapter protein coupling FFAR4 receptor to specific downstream signaling pathways, as well as mediating receptor endocytosis. During the activation step of NLRP3 inflammasome, directly associates with NLRP3 leading to inhibition of pro-inflammatory cytokine release and inhibition of inflammation.

gene.name: basigin (Ok blood group)
gene.function: Essential for normal retinal maturation and development (By similarity). Acts as a retinal cell surface receptor for NXNL1 and plays an important role in NXNL1-mediated survival of retinal cone photoreceptors. In association with glucose transporter SLC16A1/GLUT1 and NXNL1, promotes retinal cone survival by enhancing aerobic glycolysis and accelerating the entry of glucose into photoreceptors. May act as a potent stimulator of IL6 secretion in multiple cell lines that include monocytes.

gene.name: cellular communication network factor 2
gene.function: Major connective tissue mitoattractant secreted by vascular endothelial cells. Promotes proliferation and differentiation of chondrocytes. Is involved in the stimulation of osteoblast differentiation and has a critical role in osteogenesis. Mediates heparin- and divalent cation-dependent cell adhesion in many cell types including fibroblasts, myofibroblasts, endothelial and epithelial cells. Enhances fibroblast growth factor- induced DNA synthesis.

gene.name: collagen type I alpha 1 chain
gene.function: Type I collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen).

gene.name: collagen type I alpha 2 chain
gene.function: Type I collagen is a member of group I collagen (fibrillar forming collagen).

gene.name: collagen type III alpha 1 chain
gene.function: Collagen type III occurs in most soft connective tissues along with type I collagen. Involved in regulation of cortical development. Is the major ligand of ADGRG1 in the developing brain and binding to ADGRG1 inhibits neuronal migration and activates the RhoA pathway by coupling ADGRG1 to GNA13 and possibly GNA12.

gene.name: cytochrome b-245 alpha chain
gene.function: Subunit of NADPH oxidase complexes that is required for the NADPH oxidase activity that generates, in various cell types, superoxide from molecular oxygen utilizing NADPH as an electron donor. Subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex that mediates the transfer of electrons from cytosolic NADPH to O2 to produce the superoxide anion (O2(-)). In the activated complex, electrons are first transferred from NADPH to flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and subsequently transferred via two heme molecules to molecular oxygen, producing superoxide through an outer-sphere reaction. Activation of the NADPH oxidase complex is initiated by the assembly of cytosolic subunits of the NADPH oxidase complex with the core NADPH oxidase complex to form a complex at the plasma membrane or phagosomal membrane. This activation process is initiated by phosphorylation dependent binding of the cytosolic NCF1/p47-phox subunit to the C-terminus of CYBA/p22-phox. Associates with NOX3 to form a functional NADPH oxidase constitutively generating superoxide.

gene.name: decorin
gene.function: May affect the rate of fibrils formation.

gene.name: dihydrofolate reductase
gene.function: Catalyzes the reduction of 7,8-dihydrofolate (DHF) to 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolate in a NADPH-dependent manner. Key enzyme in folate metabolism. Contributes to the nuclear and mitochondrial de novo thymidylate biosynthesis pathway. Catalyzes an essential reaction for de novo glycine and purine synthesis, and for DNA precursor synthesis. Binds its own mRNA and that of DHFR2.

gene.name: epidermal growth factor receptor
gene.function: Receptor tyrosine kinase binding ligands of the EGF family and activating several signaling cascades to convert extracellular cues into appropriate cellular responses. Known ligands include EGF, TGFA/TGF-alpha, AREG, epigen/EPGN, BTC/betacellulin, epiregulin/EREG and HBEGF/heparin-binding EGF. Ligand binding triggers receptor homo- and/or heterodimerization and autophosphorylation on key cytoplasmic residues. The phosphorylated receptor recruits adapter proteins like GRB2 which in turn activates complex downstream signaling cascades. Activates at least 4 major downstream signaling cascades including the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK, PI3 kinase-AKT, PLCgamma-PKC and STATs modules. May also activate the NF-kappa-B signaling cascade. Also directly phosphorylates other proteins like RGS16, activating its GTPase activity and probably coupling the EGF receptor signaling to the G protein-coupled receptor signaling. Also phosphorylates MUC1 and increases its interaction with SRC and CTNNB1/beta-catenin. Positively regulates cell migration via interaction with CCDC88A/GIV which retains EGFR at the cell membrane following ligand stimulation, promoting EGFR signaling which triggers cell migration. Acts as a positive regulator of cGAS-STING signaling by mediating tyrosine phosphorylation of STING1, promoting production of type I interferon (IFN-alpha and IFN-beta), while inhibiting STING1 ability to regulate autophagy. Plays a role in enhancing learning and memory performance (By similarity). Plays a role in mammalian pain signaling (long-lasting hypersensitivity) (By similarity).

gene.name: elastin
gene.function: Major structural protein of tissues such as aorta and nuchal ligament, which must expand rapidly and recover completely. Molecular determinant of the late arterial morphogenesis, stabilizing arterial structure by regulating proliferation and organization of vascular smooth muscle (By similarity). .

gene.name: fibrillin 1
gene.function: Structural component of the 10-12 nm diameter microfibrils of the extracellular matrix, which conveys both structural and regulatory properties to load-bearing connective tissues. Fibrillin-1-containing microfibrils provide long-term force bearing structural support. In tissues such as the lung, blood vessels and skin, microfibrils form the periphery of the elastic fiber, acting as a scaffold for the deposition of elastin. In addition, microfibrils can occur as elastin-independent networks in tissues such as the ciliary zonule, tendon, cornea and glomerulus where they provide tensile strength and have anchoring roles. Fibrillin-1 also plays a key role in tissue homeostasis through specific interactions with growth factors, such as the bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), growth and differentiation factors (GDFs) and latent transforming growth factor-beta-binding proteins (LTBPs), cell-surface integrins and other extracellular matrix protein and proteoglycan components. Regulates osteoblast maturation by controlling TGF- beta bioavailability and calibrating TGF-beta and BMP levels, respectively (By similarity). Negatively regulates osteoclastogenesis by binding and sequestering an osteoclast differentiation and activation factor TNFSF11. This leads to disruption of TNFSF11-induced Ca(2+) signaling and impairment of TNFSF11-mediated nuclear translocation and activation of transcription factor NFATC1 which regulates genes important for osteoclast differentiation and function. Mediates cell adhesion via its binding to cell surface receptors integrins ITGAV:ITGB3 and ITGA5:ITGB1. Binds heparin and this interaction has an important role in the assembly of microfibrils.

gene.name: fibrillin 2
gene.function: Fibrillins are structural components of 10-12 nm extracellular calcium-binding microfibrils, which occur either in association with elastin or in elastin-free bundles. Fibrillin-2- containing microfibrils regulate the early process of elastic fiber assembly. Regulates osteoblast maturation by controlling TGF-beta bioavailability and calibrating TGF-beta and BMP levels, respectively. .

gene.name: integrin subunit alpha 7
gene.function: Integrin alpha-7/beta-1 is the primary laminin receptor on skeletal myoblasts and adult myofibers. During myogenic differentiation, it may induce changes in the shape and mobility of myoblasts, and facilitate their localization at laminin-rich sites of secondary fiber formation. It is involved in the maintenance of the myofibers cytoarchitecture as well as for their anchorage, viability and functional integrity. Isoform Alpha-7X2B and isoform Alpha-7X1B promote myoblast migration on laminin 1 and laminin 2/4, but isoform Alpha-7X1B is less active on laminin 1 (In vitro). Acts as a Schwann cell receptor for laminin-2. Acts as a receptor of COMP and mediates its effect on vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) maturation (By similarity). Required to promote contractile phenotype acquisition in differentiated airway smooth muscle (ASM) cells.

gene.name: lysyl oxidase
gene.function: Responsible for the post-translational oxidative deamination of peptidyl lysine residues in precursors to fibrous collagen and elastin. Regulator of Ras expression. May play a role in tumor suppression. Plays a role in the aortic wall architecture (By similarity).

gene.name: matrix metallopeptidase 2
gene.function: Ubiquitinous metalloproteinase that is involved in diverse functions such as remodeling of the vasculature, angiogenesis, tissue repair, tumor invasion, inflammation, and atherosclerotic plaque rupture. As well as degrading extracellular matrix proteins, can also act on several nonmatrix proteins such as big endothelial 1 and beta- type CGRP promoting vasoconstriction. Also cleaves KISS at a Gly-|-Leu bond. Appears to have a role in myocardial cell death pathways. Contributes to myocardial oxidative stress by regulating the activity of GSK3beta. Cleaves GSK3beta in vitro. Involved in the formation of the fibrovascular tissues in association with MMP14.

gene.name: matrix metallopeptidase 9
gene.function: Matrix metalloproteinase that plays an essential role in local proteolysis of the extracellular matrix and in leukocyte migration. Could play a role in bone osteoclastic resorption (By similarity). Cleaves KiSS1 at a Gly-|-Leu bond. Cleaves NINJ1 to generate the Secreted ninjurin-1 form. Cleaves type IV and type V collagen into large C-terminal three quarter fragments and shorter N- terminal one quarter fragments. Degrades fibronectin but not laminin or Pz-peptide.

gene.name: myosin heavy chain 11
gene.function: Muscle contraction.

gene.name: myocardin
gene.function: Smooth muscle cells (SM) and cardiac muscle cells-specific transcriptional factor which uses the canonical single or multiple CArG boxes DNA sequence. Acts as a cofactor of serum response factor (SRF) with the potential to modulate SRF-target genes. Plays a crucial role in cardiogenesis, urinary bladder development, and differentiation of the smooth muscle cell lineage (myogenesis) (By similarity). Positively regulates the transcription of genes involved in vascular smooth muscle contraction (By similarity).

gene.name: NADPH oxidase 4
gene.function: NADPH oxidase that catalyzes predominantly the reduction of oxygen to H2O2. Can also catalyze to a smaller extent, the reduction of oxygen to superoxide. May function as an oxygen sensor regulating the KCNK3/TASK-1 potassium channel and HIF1A activity. May regulate insulin signaling cascade. May play a role in apoptosis, bone resorption and lipolysaccharide-mediated activation of NFKB. May produce superoxide in the nucleus and play a role in regulating gene expression upon cell stimulation. Promotes ferroptosis, reactive oxygen species production and reduced glutathione (GSH) levels by activating NLRP3 inflammasome activation and cytokine release.

gene.name: SKI proto-oncogene
gene.function: May play a role in terminal differentiation of skeletal muscle cells but not in the determination of cells to the myogenic lineage. Functions as a repressor of TGF-beta signaling. .

gene.name: SMAD family member 2
gene.function: Receptor-regulated SMAD (R-SMAD) that is an intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) and activin type 1 receptor kinases. Binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD2/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription. Promotes TGFB1-mediated transcription of odontoblastic differentiation genes in dental papilla cells (By similarity). Positively regulates PDPK1 kinase activity by stimulating its dissociation from the 14-3-3 protein YWHAQ which acts as a negative regulator. May act as a tumor suppressor in colorectal carcinoma.

gene.name: SMAD family member 3
gene.function: Receptor-regulated SMAD (R-SMAD) that is an intracellular signal transducer and transcriptional modulator activated by TGF-beta (transforming growth factor) and activin type 1 receptor kinases. Binds the TRE element in the promoter region of many genes that are regulated by TGF-beta and, on formation of the SMAD3/SMAD4 complex, activates transcription. Also can form a SMAD3/SMAD4/JUN/FOS complex at the AP- 1/SMAD site to regulate TGF-beta-mediated transcription. Has an inhibitory effect on wound healing probably by modulating both growth and migration of primary keratinocytes and by altering the TGF-mediated chemotaxis of monocytes. This effect on wound healing appears to be hormone-sensitive. Regulator of chondrogenesis and osteogenesis and inhibits early healing of bone fractures. Positively regulates PDPK1 kinase activity by stimulating its dissociation from the 14-3-3 protein YWHAQ which acts as a negative regulator.

gene.name: transforming growth factor beta 1
gene.function: Transforming growth factor beta-1 proprotein: Precursor of the Latency-associated peptide (LAP) and Transforming growth factor beta-1 (TGF-beta-1) chains, which constitute the regulatory and active subunit of TGF-beta-1, respectively.

gene.name: transforming growth factor beta 2
gene.function: Precursor of the Latency-associated peptide (LAP) and Transforming growth factor beta-2 (TGF-beta-2) chains, which constitute the regulatory and active subunit of TGF-beta-2, respectively.

gene.name: transforming growth factor beta receptor 1
gene.function: Transmembrane serine/threonine kinase forming with the TGF- beta type II serine/threonine kinase receptor, TGFBR2, the non- promiscuous receptor for the TGF-beta cytokines TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3. Transduces the TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and is thus regulating a plethora of physiological and pathological processes including cell cycle arrest in epithelial and hematopoietic cells, control of mesenchymal cell proliferation and differentiation, wound healing, extracellular matrix production, immunosuppression and carcinogenesis. The formation of the receptor complex composed of 2 TGFBR1 and 2 TGFBR2 molecules symmetrically bound to the cytokine dimer results in the phosphorylation and the activation of TGFBR1 by the constitutively active TGFBR2. Activated TGFBR1 phosphorylates SMAD2 which dissociates from the receptor and interacts with SMAD4. The SMAD2-SMAD4 complex is subsequently translocated to the nucleus where it modulates the transcription of the TGF-beta-regulated genes. This constitutes the canonical SMAD-dependent TGF-beta signaling cascade. Also involved in non-canonical, SMAD-independent TGF-beta signaling pathways. For instance, TGFBR1 induces TRAF6 autoubiquitination which in turn results in MAP3K7 ubiquitination and activation to trigger apoptosis. Also regulates epithelial to mesenchymal transition through a SMAD- independent signaling pathway through PARD6A phosphorylation and activation.

gene.name: transforming growth factor beta receptor 2
gene.function: Transmembrane serine/threonine kinase forming with the TGF- beta type I serine/threonine kinase receptor, TGFBR1, the non- promiscuous receptor for the TGF-beta cytokines TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3. Transduces the TGFB1, TGFB2 and TGFB3 signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and thus regulates a plethora of physiological and pathological processes including cell cycle arrest in epithelial and hematopoietic cells, control of mesenchymal cell proliferation and differentiation, wound healing, extracellular matrix production, immunosuppression and carcinogenesis. The formation of the receptor complex composed of 2 TGFBR1 and 2 TGFBR2 molecules symmetrically bound to the cytokine dimer results in the phosphorylation and activation of TGFBR1 by the constitutively active TGFBR2. Activated TGFBR1 phosphorylates SMAD2 which dissociates from the receptor and interacts with SMAD4. The SMAD2-SMAD4 complex is subsequently translocated to the nucleus where it modulates the transcription of the TGF-beta-regulated genes. This constitutes the canonical SMAD-dependent TGF-beta signaling cascade. Also involved in non-canonical, SMAD-independent TGF-beta signaling pathways. .
gene.target_class: TKL protein kinase STKR Type 2 subfamily

gene.name: thrombospondin 1
gene.function: Adhesive glycoprotein that mediates cell-to-cell and cell-to- matrix interactions. Multifunctional, involved in inflammation, angiogenesis, wound healing, reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling, nitrous oxide (NO) signaling, apoptosis, senescence, aging, cellular self-renewal, stemness, and cardiovascular and metabolic homeostasis. Negatively modulates dendritic cell activation and cytokine release, as part of an autocrine feedback loop, contributing to the resolution of inflammation and immune homeostasis. Ligand for receptor CD47. Modulates nitrous oxide (NO) signaling via CD47, hence playing a role as a pressor agent, supporting blood pressure (By similarity). Plays a role in endothelial cell senescence, acting via CD47, by increasing the abundance and activation of NADPH oxidase NOX1, and so generating excess ROS. Inhibits stem cell self-renewal, acting via CD47 signaling, probably by regulation of the stem cell transcription factors POU5F1/OCT4, SOX2, MYC/c-Myc and KLF4 (By similarity). Negatively modulates wound healing, acting via CD47 (By similarity). Ligand for receptor CD36. Involved in inducing apoptosis in podocytes in response to elevated free fatty acids, acting via CD36 (By similarity). Plays a role in suppressing angiogenesis, acting, depending on context, via CD36 or CD47. Promotes cellular senescence in a TP53-CDKN1A-RB1 signaling-dependent manner. Ligand for immunoglobulin-like cell surface receptor SIRPA. Involved in ROS signaling in non- phagocytic cells, stimulating NADPH oxidase-derived ROS production, acting via interaction with SIRPA. Plays a role in metabolic dysfunction in diet-induced obesity, perhaps acting by exacerbating adipose inflammatory activity; its effects may be mediated, at least in part, through enhanced adipocyte proliferation (By similarity). Plays a role in ER stress response, via its interaction with the activating transcription factor 6 alpha (ATF6) which produces adaptive ER stress response factors (By similarity). May be involved in age-related conditions, including metabolic dysregulation, during normal aging.

papers.title: Everolimus Rescues the Phenotype of Elastin Insufficiency in Patient Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells.
papers.summary: In patient iPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells modeling Williams syndrome or nonsyndromic ELN-associated elastin insufficiency, everolimus most consistently improved impaired differentiation, hyperproliferation, and endothelin-induced calcium flux. The findings support repurposing everolimus for elastin-insufficiency vasculopathy, but clinical efficacy in patients was not tested, and the paper does not establish efficacy in Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: Everolimus rescued vascular smooth muscle abnormalities in elastin-insufficiency patient cells, offering a tested drug-repurposing precedent for related Marfan VSMC and aortic phenotypes.

papers.title: Comparison of the Effect of Aliskiren Versus Negative Controls on Aortic Stiffness in Patients With Marfan Syndrome Under Treatment With Atenolol.
papers.summary: In 28 patients with Marfan syndrome receiving atenolol, adding aliskiren for 24 weeks did not significantly improve MRI-measured central aortic distensibility or central pulsed wave velocity compared with no additional aliskiren. Peripheral brachial-ankle pulsed wave velocity decreased significantly, while central systolic aortic blood pressure showed a nonsignificant tendency to be lower.
papers.why: A randomized trial in Marfan patients directly evaluated aliskiren added to atenolol and measured central and peripheral aortic vascular endpoints, finding no significant central stiffness benefit but a peripheral pulse-wave velocity effect.

papers.title: COMPARE and Pediatric Heart Network Investigator trials: Losartan finally validated in humans with Marfan, but much work remains!
papers.summary: The paper synthesizes animal evidence and two randomized human trials showing that losartan slows aortic root enlargement in Marfan syndrome, although its advantage over atenolol and effects beyond the aortic root remain unproven. The authors regard losartan as a safe therapeutic option, particularly for patients unable to tolerate β-blockers, while emphasizing unresolved questions about optimal timing, dose, patient selection, and combination therapy.
papers.why: The paper summarizes randomized human trials directly testing losartan and atenolol for prevention of aortic dilation in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Long-term clinical outcomes of losartan in patients with Marfan syndrome: follow-up of the multicentre randomized controlled COMPARE trial.
papers.summary: In a retrospective long-term follow-up of the COMPARE trial, continuous losartan use was associated with fewer deaths, aortic dissections, and combined clinical events in adults with Marfan syndrome over approximately 8 years. Root replacement, reoperation, and vascular graft implantation were not significantly reduced, and the findings support losartan, preferably combined with a β-blocker, as an acceptable but not conclusively established treatment option.
papers.why: Long-term COMPARE follow-up found fewer deaths, dissections, and composite cardiovascular events among continuous losartan users than among untreated controls.

papers.title: Rationale and design of a trial evaluating the effects of losartan vs. nebivolol vs. the association of both on the progression of aortic root dilation in Marfan syndrome with FBN1 gene mutations.
papers.summary: This paper describes an ongoing open-label phase III trial comparing losartan, nebivolol, and their combination in 291 patients with Marfan syndrome and FBN1 mutations who have aortic root dilation. The study is designed to assess aortic root growth and explore pharmacokinetic, pharmacogenetic, transcriptomic, and TGF-beta mechanisms, but it reports no trial results.
papers.why: This Marfan trial protocol specifies three pharmacological strategies and a multiparametric endpoint and biomarker framework for predicting aortic response.

papers.title: Effect of perindopril on large artery stiffness and aortic root diameter in patients with Marfan syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a small randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, perindopril added to standard beta-blocker therapy reduced arterial stiffness, central and peripheral pulse wave velocity, and aortic root diameter in 17 patients with Marfan syndrome. Perindopril also reduced latent and active transforming growth factor beta levels, with the authors proposing reduced TGF-beta signaling as a possible mechanism, but the trial was small and the publication was retracted.
papers.why: A small randomized trial reported that perindopril reduced arterial stiffness and aortic root diameter in beta-blocked Marfan patients, although the publication is retracted.

papers.title: In vivo characterization of doxycycline-mediated protection of aortic function and structure in a mouse model of Marfan syndrome-associated aortic aneurysm.
papers.summary: In a Fbn1C1039G/+ mouse model of Marfan syndrome, long-term sub-antimicrobial doxycycline reduced aortic root dilation, normalized left ventricular mass, lowered aortic pulse wave velocity, decreased MMP-2 and MMP-9 expression, and improved elastic-fiber integrity. The findings provide preclinical proof of concept for matrix metalloproteinase inhibition, but doxycycline was not tested in patients with Marfan syndrome, and residual stiffness and morphologic abnormalities remained in older mice.
papers.why: The mouse intervention study demonstrates that doxycycline reduces aortic-root growth, improves aortic elasticity, and corrects elastic-fiber abnormalities in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Irbesartan in Marfan syndrome (AIMS): a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial.
papers.summary: The AIMS randomised trial found that irbesartan reduced the annual rate of aortic root dilatation in children and young adults with Marfan syndrome compared with placebo over a median of 4 years. The treatment was well tolerated, with no observed difference in serious adverse events, but the trial was not powered to establish effects on clinical outcomes.
papers.why: A randomized placebo-controlled trial in 192 people with Marfan syndrome showed that irbesartan reduced annual aortic root dilatation over up to five years.

papers.title: Angiotensin receptor blockers and β blockers in Marfan syndrome: an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials.
papers.summary: Individual patient data from seven randomised trials showed that angiotensin receptor blockers approximately halved progressive aortic root enlargement in patients with Marfan syndrome who had not undergone prior aortic surgery, including among patients already taking a β blocker. β blockers had a similar estimated effect, but their evidence was indirect, and neither treatment class showed a detectable reduction in aortic dissection, aortic root surgery, or death during the relatively short trials.
papers.why: Individual-patient meta-analysis of randomized trials provides comparative efficacy data for ARBs and beta blockers in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Marfan syndrome: current perspectives.
papers.summary: This review summarizes clinical, mechanistic, genetic, imaging, biomarker, and therapeutic findings in Marfan syndrome, emphasizing that losartan responses vary by FBN1 mutation mechanism and that beta-receptor blockers remain first-line therapy. It also identifies investigational candidates such as FBN1 mutation analysis, multigene next-generation sequencing, total homocysteine, TGF-β1, oxidative-stress markers, and lysyl oxidase, while emphasizing unresolved genotype–phenotype interpretation and limited prospective validation.
papers.why: The review summarizes Marfan-specific losartan trials, beta-blocker practice, aortic outcomes, and candidate biochemical markers for disease progression.

papers.title: Management Strategies of Ocular Abnormalities in Patients with Marfan Syndrome: Current Perspective.
papers.summary: This review describes how fibrillin-1–related connective-tissue abnormalities cause characteristic ocular disease in Marfan syndrome, particularly zonular weakness, ectopia lentis, refractive impairment, amblyopia, retinal detachment, cataract, and glaucoma. It reports current management approaches, including refractive correction, lens extraction with intraocular lens implantation, retinal-detachment surgery, and glaucoma treatment, while emphasizing procedural complications and the need for long-term follow-up.
papers.why: This review describes existing refractive and surgical management strategies for Marfan-associated ectopia lentis, including reported visual outcomes and unresolved safety questions.

papers.title: Gene panel sequencing in heritable thoracic aortic disorders and related entities - results of comprehensive testing in a cohort of 264 patients.
papers.summary: A seven-gene next-generation sequencing panel identified pathogenic variants in 13% of 264 unrelated probands with heritable thoracic aortic disorders or related phenotypes. Panel testing established a Marfan syndrome diagnosis in 10 FBN1-positive patients, including patients who did not meet the revised Ghent criteria or had overlapping syndromic features, but it missed large deletions or insertions and therefore required complementary testing in strongly suspicious cases.
papers.why: The cohort demonstrates that targeted multigene panel sequencing efficiently detects causal variants in Marfan and related hereditary thoracic aortic disorders, including patients with atypical or non-MFS phenotypes.

papers.title: Targeted deletion of fibrillin-1 in the mouse eye results in ectopia lentis and other ocular phenotypes associated with Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: Conditional deletion of Fbn1 in the mouse non-pigmented ciliary epithelium, but not lens, markedly weakens and thins ciliary zonular fibers and produces ectopia lentis, followed by cataract and buphthalmia. The model reproduces important ocular manifestations of Marfan syndrome and provides quantitative structural and biomechanical endpoints for testing interventions intended to preserve or strengthen the zonule.
papers.why: The tissue-specific mouse knockout reproduces ectopia lentis, zonular rupture, cataract, and abnormal eye growth, making it a reusable model of Marfan-related ocular disease.

papers.title: Targeting feed-forward signaling of TGFβ/NOX4/DHFR/eNOS uncoupling/TGFβ axis with anti-TGFβ and folic acid attenuates formation of aortic aneurysms: Novel mechanisms and therapeutics.
papers.summary: In Fbn1C1039G/+ Marfan syndrome mice, the paper identifies a feed-forward TGFβ/NOX4/DHFR/eNOS-uncoupling pathway that promotes aortic aneurysm formation. Anti-TGFβ and folic acid attenuated aneurysm expansion by restoring DHFR and tetrahydrobiopterin availability, reducing reactive oxygen species, and recoupling eNOS, while circulating H4B was proposed as a biomarker of aneurysm size.
papers.why: The study directly tests disease-modifying treatments in Marfan mice and reports both reduced aneurysm formation and a validated candidate biomarker of aortic tissue tetrahydrobiopterin availability.

papers.title: Single-Cell Analysis of Aneurysmal Aortic Tissue in Patients with Marfan Syndrome Reveals Dysfunctional TGF-β Signaling.
papers.summary: Single-cell transcriptomic and immunostaining analyses of advanced aneurysmal ascending aortic tissue from three patients with Marfan syndrome found increased de-differentiated, proliferative smooth muscle cells despite increased TGFB1 expression. The study identified reduced expression of canonical TGF-β receptors, SMAD proteins, and mature smooth-muscle contractile markers, while finding little evidence for increased non-canonical TGF-β signaling.
papers.why: The study directly applies single-cell RNA sequencing and immunostaining to Marfan aortic aneurysms, yielding reusable cell-state and TGF-β signaling data and assays.

papers.title: The importance of genotype-phenotype correlation in the clinical management of Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 90 patients with FBN1 variants and suspected Marfan syndrome, FBN1 genotype was associated with phenotype: missense variants were associated with more ectopia lentis, whereas truncating variants were associated with substantially more aortic events. The findings support FBN1 testing and modified Ghent diagnostic criteria for diagnosis and risk stratification, and the study reports favorable short-term use of valve-sparing aortic root replacement in selected operated patients.
papers.why: Prospective Marfan cohort data show that truncating FBN1 variants are associated with substantially more aortic events than missense variants, supporting genotype-guided risk management.

papers.title: Transforming Growth Factor-β and the Renin-Angiotensin System in Syndromic Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: Implications for Treatment.
papers.summary: This review identifies excessive, developmentally timed TGF-β signaling and renin-angiotensin system (RAS) activation as contributors to syndromic thoracic aortic aneurysm pathology, particularly in Marfan syndrome. It reports that TGF-β neutralization, angiotensin receptor blockers, β-blockers, ERK1/2 inhibition, and doxycycline can attenuate aortic disease in preclinical models, while clinical ARB and β-blocker trials in Marfan syndrome show mixed effects on aortic growth and insufficient evidence for major clinical outcomes.
papers.why: The review summarizes clinical-trial evidence for ARBs and beta-blockers in syndromic thoracic aortic aneurysm, explicitly including Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: AGGF1 therapy inhibits thoracic aortic aneurysms by enhancing integrin α7-mediated inhibition of TGF-β1 maturation and ERK1/2 signaling.
papers.summary: In the Fbn1C1041G/+ mouse model of Marfan syndrome-associated thoracic aortic aneurysm, intraperitoneal AGGF1 protein reduced aortic dilatation, vascular remodeling, inflammation, mature TGF-β1, and ERK1/2 and Smad2/3 phosphorylation. The proposed mechanism is AGGF1 binding to VSMC integrin α7 and enhancing its interaction with LAP-TGF-β1, thereby inhibiting TGF-β1 maturation; efficacy was demonstrated only in mice and was lost with the receptor-binding-deficient AGGF1-RDDdel mutant.
papers.why: AGGF1 and pirfenidone were tested across aortic aneurysm models including Fbn1 C1041G/+ mice and reduced inflammation, remodeling, and aortic disease through defined signaling mechanisms.

papers.title: Optimising the mutation screening strategy in Marfan syndrome and identifying genotypes with more severe aortic involvement.
papers.summary: In a two-phase observational study of 136 patients with clinically diagnosed Marfan syndrome or Marfanoid habitus, sequencing followed by multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification identified pathogenic variants in 62%, including 78 FBN1 variants and 6 variants associated with Loeys-Dietz syndrome. FBN1 dominant-negative variants eliminating a disulphide-bonding cysteine were associated with more frequent ectopia lentis, aortic involvement, and aortic surgery, supporting genotype-informed cardiovascular risk stratification but requiring prospective validation.
papers.why: This Marfan study validates combined NGS, gene-panel, and MLPA testing and identifies FBN1 mutation classes associated with higher aortic involvement.

papers.title: Generation of heterozygous fibrillin-1 mutant cloned pigs from genome-edited foetal fibroblasts.
papers.summary: The study generated heterozygous FBN1-mutant cloned pigs and showed that they develop selected Marfan syndrome-like phenotypes, including skeletal abnormalities, scoliosis, and disrupted proximal aortic elastic fibres. Phenotypic variability, absence of aortic dilation and ectopia lentis in heterozygotes, and more extensive vascular, ocular, and skeletal disease with neonatal lethality in homozygotes indicate that the model is useful but incompletely recapitulates human Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: The study generates a heterozygous FBN1-mutant pig model with human-like skeletal and aortic phenotypes suitable for Marfan pathogenesis studies and treatment development.

papers.title: The revised role of TGF-β in aortic aneurysms in Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: In a substudy of 99 adults with Marfan syndrome, plasma transforming growth factor-β was higher than in healthy controls, but losartan did not lower it overall after one month and the direction of change was paradoxically associated with subsequent aortic root dilatation. The authors therefore propose that plasma transforming growth factor-β is primarily a readout of aortic disease, whereas increased angiotensin II–mediated signaling may initiate aortic dilatation.
papers.why: Reports in Marfan syndrome that changes in plasma TGF-beta correlate with losartan response and aortic root dilation, providing a candidate pharmacodynamic biomarker.

papers.title: Targeted gene panel sequencing for the rapid diagnosis of acutely ill infants.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 20 critically ill infants, the rapid targeted gene panel RapSeq identified a de novo pathogenic FBN1 variant consistent with Marfan syndrome in one neonate presenting with cardiac and respiratory failure, poly-valvular dysplasia, and multiple joint contractures. The diagnosis enabled early and precise clinical management, although the study was limited by its small cohort and the inability of this version of RapSeq to detect copy-number aberrations.
papers.why: The rapid sequencing panel identified an FBN1 diagnosis in an acutely ill neonate and changed clinical management, directly supporting diagnosis of neonatal Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Increased frequency of FBN1 frameshift and nonsense mutations in Marfan syndrome patients with aortic dissection.
papers.summary: In 180 Chinese patients with Marfan syndrome, FBN1 frameshift and nonsense variants were more frequent among patients with aortic dissection than among those with aortic aneurysm, whereas missense variants were more frequent with aneurysm. Surgical aortic-wall specimens associated with frameshift and nonsense variants showed more severe degeneration, fibrosis, elastic-fiber disruption, and fewer or more disorganized smooth muscle cells, but the proposed molecular mechanism remains unvalidated.
papers.why: In 180 Marfan patients, the study identifies FBN1 frameshift and nonsense mutations as markers more frequently associated with aortic dissection and provides data relevant to treatment risk assessment.

papers.title: Medical treatment of aortic aneurysms in Marfan syndrome and other heritable conditions.
papers.summary: This review concludes that medical therapy for aortic aneurysms in Marfan syndrome is not yet optimized: β-blockers have limited and inconsistent evidence, while losartan reduces aortic dilation in animal models and small human cohorts, but definitive effects on dissection and mortality remain unproven. Experimental approaches include ERK inhibition, MMP inhibition with doxycycline, and genotype-guided treatment, but most require further validation before clinical translation.
papers.why: Reviews medical treatments for Marfan-associated aortic aneurysm, including losartan and beta-blockers, and summarizes human and experimental supporting evidence.

papers.title: Genetic testing of 248 Chinese aortopathy patients using a panel assay.
papers.summary: In 248 Chinese probands with Marfan syndrome or related aortic disease, a 15-gene next-generation sequencing panel identified a likely pathogenic variant in 37.1%, most often in FBN1, while the optimized iAorta pipeline reduced the false-positive rate from 25.4% to 15.4%. FBN1 truncating or splicing variants were associated with more severe aortic or valvular disease and earlier prophylactic surgery, although variant interpretation remained limited by incomplete clinical information and insufficient functional evidence.
papers.why: The study validates a targeted aortopathy panel in Chinese patients with aortic disease or Marfan syndrome and provides both diagnostic data and improved analysis quality control.

papers.title: The Effect of a Nonpeptide Angiotensin II Type 2 Receptor Agonist, Compound 21, on Aortic Aneurysm Growth in a Mouse Model of Marfan Syndrome.
papers.summary: In male Fbn1C1039G/+ mice modeling Marfan syndrome, losartan reduced aortic root growth, whereas the selective AT2R agonist Compound 21, enalapril, and their combinations showed no aortic-growth benefit at the tested doses and routes. No treatment significantly improved the quantified aortic histopathology, and earlier C21 initiation also failed to show benefit.
papers.why: The study directly tests established and experimental renin-angiotensin-system drugs in a Marfan mouse model using aortic imaging and histopathology.

papers.title: No beneficial effect of general and specific anti-inflammatory therapies on aortic dilatation in Marfan mice.
papers.summary: In adult FBN1 C1039G/+ mice with established aortic root dilatation, losartan reduced leukocyte and macrophage infiltration, nuclear pSmad2, and aortic root dilatation, whereas methylprednisolone and abatacept reduced macrophage infiltration without slowing dilatation. Methylprednisolone additionally increased Alcian blue-positive damage, indicating that broad or macrophage-directed anti-inflammatory treatment may not improve—and may worsen—aortic pathology in this model.
papers.why: The controlled animal experiment directly compares existing anti-inflammatory treatments with losartan and shows efficacy data for aortic-root dilation in a Marfan model.

papers.title: A microfibril assembly assay identifies different mechanisms of dominance underlying Marfan syndrome, stiff skin syndrome and acromelic dysplasias.
papers.summary: A full-length GFP-tagged fibrillin-1 secretion and microfibril incorporation assay distinguishes the dominant molecular mechanisms of TB4/TB5-domain fibrillinopathies. Marfan syndrome-associated FBN1 variants showed reduced extracellular protein and absent microfibril incorporation, whereas stiff skin syndrome and acromelic dysplasia variants were generally secreted and assembled like wild type, supporting different downstream mechanisms of TGFβ dysregulation.
papers.why: The paper develops and validates a functional assay for fibrillin-1 variants that directly distinguishes pathogenic mechanisms in Marfan syndrome and related fibrillinopathies.

papers.title: Visual outcome and surgical results in children with Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: In this retrospective observational study of 41 children with genetically confirmed Marfan syndrome, bilateral lens subluxation was common, and 52% of affected children were referred for lensectomy. Visual acuity improved after lensectomy, with no observed retinal detachment, although one patient developed macular oedema requiring intravitreal steroids and another required repositioning of an Artisan intraocular lens.
papers.why: The retrospective study reports lensectomy outcomes and visual-acuity improvement in children with genetically confirmed Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: AP-1 Oligodeoxynucleotides Reduce Aortic Elastolysis in a Murine Model of Marfan Syndrome.
papers.summary: In the mgR/mgR murine model of Marfan syndrome, AP-1 neutralization with consensus decoy oligodeoxynucleotides reduced MMP-2/MMP-9 expression and activity, smooth-muscle-cell migration and reactive oxygen species formation, and ex vivo pretreated aortic-graft elastolysis, MMP activity, and macrophage infiltration. The study also showed increased aortic endothelial permeability in Marfan mice, which facilitated dODN penetration into the aortic media, but did not test treatment efficacy in patients with Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: Reports an experimentally tested gene-silencing strategy that reduces elastolysis, MMP activity and aneurysm-related changes in a murine Marfan model.

papers.title: Dissecting aortic aneurysm in Marfan syndrome is associated with losartan-sensitive transcriptomic modulation of aortic cells.
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified two mutant-specific aortic cell subpopulations, SMC3 and EC4, that were combined as an MFS-modulated population associated with dissecting thoracic aortic aneurysm in Fbn1mgR/mgR mice. The MFSmod population localized to the intima, resembled human thoracic aortic aneurysm smooth-muscle-derived clusters, and was suppressed by losartan together with downregulation of extracellular-matrix genes; the study did not establish whether MFSmod is a cause or consequence of disease.
papers.why: This study provides direct evidence in a Marfan mouse model that losartan eliminates disease-associated aortic cell states identified by single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretation and classification of FBN1 variants associated with Marfan syndrome: consensus recommendations from the Clinical Genome Resource's FBN1 variant curation expert panel.
papers.summary: The paper establishes FBN1-specific adaptations of the ACMG/AMP criteria for classifying variants associated with Marfan syndrome and provides criteria based on population frequency, phenotype, segregation, computational predictions, and functional evidence. In a pilot study of 60 variants, the specifications reduced variants of uncertain significance from 24 to 12 and achieved 85.0% classification concordance among participating institutions.
papers.why: The consensus provides disease-specific criteria and functional-assay guidance for interpreting and classifying FBN1 variants in Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Targeted genetic analysis in a large cohort of familial and sporadic cases of aneurysm or dissection of the thoracic aorta.
papers.summary: The study used targeted PCR and next-generation sequencing of 15 TAAD-associated genes in 1,025 unrelated familial or sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection cases. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were found in 4.9% of analyzable cases, predominantly in FBN1, and FBN1 variants were identified in patients with and without clinical Marfan syndrome, supporting genetic testing for TAAD and transferability of the FBN1-mediated mechanism to Marfan syndrome research.
papers.why: A validated targeted sequencing panel identifies causal variants and risk factors in thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection, including syndromic Marfan phenotypes.

papers.title: Next-generation sequencing for diagnosis of thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections: diagnostic yield, novel mutations and genotype phenotype correlations.
papers.summary: The study found causative or likely causative variants in 18 of 51 unrelated patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections (TAAD), including eight FBN1 variants, and showed that genotype-positive patients had shorter event-free survival than genotype-negative patients. Among the analyzed genes, defects in TGF-beta signaling were associated with the shortest event-free survival, whereas the FBN1 subgroup did not differ significantly from the reference group.
papers.why: The study demonstrates targeted NGS for genetically heterogeneous thoracic aortic disease overlapping Marfan syndrome and reports diagnostic yield and genotype-associated aortic outcomes.

papers.title: Marfan syndrome in adolescence: adolescents' perspectives on (physical) functioning, disability, contextual factors and support needs.
papers.summary: This qualitative study of 19 adolescents with Marfan syndrome found perceived activity and participation limitations, difficulty keeping up with peers, and a sense of being physically different because of appearance, pain, fatigue, and disability. The authors derived an adolescent Marfan syndrome-specific International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health for Children and Youth model to organize functioning, disability, contextual barriers and facilitators, and individual support needs.
papers.why: Patient interviews directly produced a Marfan-specific functioning, disability, and contextual-factor outcome model for adolescents.

papers.title: An Overview of Investigational and Experimental Drug Treatment Strategies for Marfan Syndrome.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the pathophysiology, established medical care, and experimental treatments for the cardiovascular manifestations of Marfan syndrome, emphasizing findings from human studies and mouse models. β-blockers and/or angiotensin receptor blockers provide clinical disease control without curing Marfan syndrome, while several experimental approaches—including TGF-β, MMP, iNOS, MAPK, androgen, GABA, and epigenetic pathway interventions—have shown preclinical benefit but limited or inconsistent translation to patients.
papers.why: The review consolidates currently used and preclinical Marfan treatments, including beta-blockers, imaging surveillance, surgery, and investigational drug approaches.

papers.title: The role of β-arrestin2-dependent signaling in thoracic aortic aneurysm formation in a murine model of Marfan syndrome.
papers.journal: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
papers.summary: In a murine Marfan syndrome model, deleting βarr2 delayed aortic root dilation and reduced ERK1/2 activation and MMP-2/-9 expression, particularly at 12–16 weeks. Mechanistic experiments in rat aortic root vascular smooth muscle cells showed that AT1aR-driven MMP-2/-9 expression requires βarr2, ERK1/2, and EGFR transactivation but not TGF-β signaling, while erlotinib blocked aortic dilation in mice.
papers.why: Directly uses Marfan mice and aortic smooth-muscle cells to demonstrate that β-arrestin2 deletion or knockdown delays aneurysm formation and identifies actionable signaling targets.

papers.title: Characterization of Two Novel Intronic Variants Affecting Splicing in FBN1-Related Disorders.
papers.summary: Two deep-intronic FBN1 variants were functionally shown to activate cryptic acceptor sites, retain intronic nucleotides, introduce premature stop codons, and produce likely truncated fibrillin 1. The c.6872-24T>A variant segregated with severe Marfan syndrome and aortic disease, whereas c.7571-12T>A was associated with MASS syndrome without observed aortic disease or ectopia lentis, illustrating the need for extended intronic sequencing and RNA-based functional assessment.
papers.why: Reports functional analysis of two FBN1 intronic variants in Marfan-related disease using mRNA studies and highlights a diagnostic workflow for interpreting intronic variants.

papers.title: Variant filtering, digenic variants, and other challenges in clinical sequencing: a lesson from fibrillinopathies.
papers.summary: The study found apparently pathogenic FBN1 variants in gnomAD at frequencies implying a Marfan syndrome predisposition of approximately 5 per 10,000 and identified two families with coexisting FBN1/FBN2 variants and mixed or amplified fibrillinopathy phenotypes. It also shows that overly strict allele-frequency filtering, incomplete manual use of ACMG/AMP criteria, and failure to consider variants in multiple genes can produce missed or variant-of-unknown-significance diagnoses.
papers.why: Provides a sequencing and variant-filtering strategy for diagnosing Marfan and related fibrillinopathies, including recognition of potentially digenic variants.

papers.title: A prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multicenter study of the effects of irbesartan on aortic dilatation in Marfan syndrome (AIMS trial): study protocol.
papers.summary: This trial protocol describes the AIMS trial, which will compare irbesartan with placebo to determine whether angiotensin II receptor blockade reduces annual aortic root dilatation in patients with Marfan syndrome. The mechanistic rationale is that abnormal fibrillin-1 causes excess extracellular TGF-β activity, while preclinical studies of Marfan mice showed that AT1 receptor blockade reduced TGF-β signaling and improved aortic-wall abnormalities; efficacy in patients remains unestablished in this protocol.
papers.why: This multicenter phase III protocol provides a ready-to-reuse clinical-trial framework and outcome assessment for testing irbesartan in Marfan-associated aortic dilation.

papers.title: Pregnancy after Aortic Root Replacement in Marfan's Syndrome: A Case Series and Review of the Literature.
papers.summary: This retrospective case series found no pregnancy-associated aortic dissections during 20 live-birth pregnancies among 14 women with Marfan syndrome after aortic root replacement, while a literature review reported dissections in 7 of 24 pregnancies. The authors conclude that residual distal aortic dissection risk is not zero, particularly after surgery for prior dissection or with residual dissection, but the exact magnitude is uncertain because the case series was small and subject to survivor and publication biases.
papers.why: This Marfan case series directly evaluates pregnancy outcomes after aortic root replacement and provides actionable counseling and risk-management information for an existing surgical therapy.

papers.title: Characterization of doxycycline-mediated inhibition of Marfan syndrome-associated aortic dilation by multiphoton microscopy.
papers.summary: Long-term doxycycline treatment improved elastic-fiber integrity, reduced MMP-2 and MMP-9 expression, prevented age-associated dermal thinning, and normalized aortic wall thickness in Fbn1C1041G/+ mice modeling Marfan syndrome. Multiphoton microscopy detected these ultrastructural changes, while total aortic elastin density and collagen content were not significantly improved and dermal thickness was proposed only as a potential marker requiring clinical validation.
papers.why: The study directly shows that doxycycline rescues aortic and dermal structural abnormalities in a Marfan mouse model and supplies imaging and molecular assessment methods.

papers.title: Impact of pathogenic FBN1 variant types on the development of severe scoliosis in patients with Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 278 patients with pathogenic or likely pathogenic FBN1 variants, protein-truncating variants and variants in the FBN1 neonatal region (exons 25–33) were independently associated with severe scoliosis in Marfan syndrome. The study suggests that FBN1 variant type and location can identify patients at increased risk of scoliosis progression, while exons 55–56 and exon 66 are proposed but unconfirmed hot spots.
papers.why: The study identifies clinically usable FBN1 genotype and patient predictors for severe and progressive scoliosis in a large Marfan syndrome cohort.

papers.title: A phenotypic screen of Marfan syndrome iPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells uncovers GSK3β as a new target.
papers.summary: A phenotypic screen of 1,022 small molecules in Marfan syndrome iPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells identified GSK3β as a recurrent drug target. In four Marfan patient-derived lines, GSK3β inhibition or knockdown reduced proteolysis and apoptosis and partially improved fibrillin-1 deposition, but did not rescue the proliferation defect and remains limited by incomplete efficacy and potential toxicity.
papers.why: The study provides a disease-specific Marfan VSMC model and identifies GSK3β inhibition as a tested strategy that improves proteolysis, apoptosis, and fibrillin-1 deposition.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas9 in zebrafish: An attractive model for FBN1 genetic defects in humans.
papers.summary: The paper generated and characterized a heterozygous fbn1 frameshift zebrafish line using CRISPR/Cas9. The mutant showed early hypopigmentation, increased body length, a slender body shape, and persistent abnormal cardiac blood flow that resembled aspects of Marfan syndrome, although retinal abnormalities were absent.
papers.why: The study generated and characterized a zebrafish model carrying an FBN1 mutation and demonstrated Marfan-like morphological and cardiovascular phenotypes.

papers.title: Exaggerated elastin turnover in young individuals with Marfan syndrome: new insights from the AIMS trial.
papers.summary: This post hoc AIMS trial analysis found that plasma desmosine, a marker of mature elastin degradation, is disproportionately elevated in children and adolescents with Marfan syndrome, coinciding with early aortic growth and dilation. The association between baseline plasma desmosine and subsequent aortic root dilation was suggestive but not statistically significant, and irbesartan had little detectable effect on plasma desmosine at one year.
papers.why: This Marfan syndrome trial analysis shows that plasma desmosine tracks elastin turnover and is associated with aortic-root dilatation, supporting an outcome biomarker for disease studies.

papers.title: New population-based exome data question the pathogenicity of some genetic variants previously associated with Marfan syndrome.
papers.summary: Population-scale exome data showed that previously reported Marfan syndrome-associated FBN1 variants occurred more frequently than expected from Marfan syndrome phenotype prevalence, raising concerns that some are benign or incompletely penetrant rather than monogenic causes. The study recommends integrating population-frequency data with computational pathogenicity prediction and clinical criteria when interpreting FBN1 variants and diagnosing Marfan syndrome.
papers.why: Population-frequency analysis and four computational predictors identified putatively overcalled FBN1 variants and provided a method for cautioning against erroneous disease stratification.

papers.title: Markers of extracellular matrix remodeling and systemic inflammation in patients with heritable thoracic aortic diseases.
papers.summary: This observational study found that plasma matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) was elevated in patients with Marfan syndrome and other heritable thoracic aortic diseases compared with healthy controls, supporting altered extracellular matrix remodeling. The study did not establish clinical diagnostic or prognostic performance, causality, or tissue-level expression of the biomarkers.
papers.why: The study directly measures extracellular-matrix and inflammatory markers in patients with Marfan syndrome and related heritable thoracic aortic diseases, identifying MMP-9 as a cross-disease candidate biomarker.

papers.title: Soluble EMMPRIN levels discriminate aortic ectasia in Marfan syndrome patients.
papers.summary: In a 42-patient observational cohort, plasma soluble EMMPRIN (sEMMPRIN) was lower in Marfan syndrome than in matched healthy controls and was selectively associated with greater aortic-root dilatation. A plasma sEMMPRIN threshold of ≤2246 pg/ml discriminated aortic ectasia with 85.7% sensitivity and 81.0% accuracy, but the authors considered these proof-of-concept findings insufficient to establish a clinical biomarker.
papers.why: Validated EMMPRIN measurements discriminated aortic ectasia in Marfan patients with 85.7% sensitivity and 76.2% specificity.

papers.title: A Randomized, Open-label, LOSARTAN Therapy on the Progression of Aortic Root Dilation in Patients With Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: To assess the efficacy of angiotensin II receptor blocker, Losartan, to prevent progressive dilation of aortic root in patients with Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Losartan Versus Atenolol for the Treatment of Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: Marfan syndrome is a genetic disease of our connective tissue, which provides material and support for our skeleton, muscles, blood vessels and other parts of our bodies. People with Marfan syndrome may be tall and thin with slender, tapering fingers, long arms and legs, and spine curvature. They often have heart and eye problems. In some patients, the condition is very mild and the person has few or no symptoms. papers.title: Atenolol Versus Losartan in the Prevention of Progressive Dilation of the Aorta in Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of Losartan versus Atenolol in the progression of aortic dilatation in patients with Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Effects of Losartan Versus Atenolol on Aortic and Cardiac Muscle Stiffness in Adults With Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: Marfan syndrome is an inherited connective tissue disorder with morbidity and mortality from aortic dilation and dissection. The degree of aortic dilation and response to beta-blockade (standard of care) vary in adults with Marfan syndrome. However, aortic stiffness is often present, and can be a predictor of aortic dilation and cardiovascular complications. In addition, adults with Marfan syndrome develop left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, which can progress to heart failure. papers.title: Measurement of Heart-carotid Pulse Wave Velocity (hcPWV) by Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV)
papers.summary:
Aortic stiffness is an important imaging biomarker of vascular aging. The ascending aorta is the most elastic segment, and it is excluded by reference non-invasive method carotid to femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV). We propose to use laser-doppler vibrometry (LDV) to record superficial vibrations generated by cardiac activity and arterial pulses for measuring heart carotid PWV, a surrogate for ascending aorta.

The trial aims to demonstrate the equivalence between heart-carotid PWV made by laser-doppler vibrometry (LDV) with the reference MRI measurement (4D-FLOW MRI).

papers.title: Angiotensin Converting Enzyme Inhibitors in Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this research is to assess the effects of a drug called perindopril on the aorta in people known to have Marfan Syndrome. The aorta is the major artery of the body that comes out of the heart and supplies blood to the body. We know that in people with Marfan Syndrome, the aorta is stiff and this stiffness results in its enlargement over many years. This enlargement of the aorta can be very serious. papers.title: Artisan Aphakia Lens for the Correction of Aphakia in Children
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety and effectiveness of the Artisan Aphakia Lens in the treatment of aphakia in children.

papers.title: Study of the Efficacy of Losartan on Aortic Dilatation in Patients With Marfan Syndrome
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate if losartan limits aortic dilatation in patients with Marfan syndrome.

papers.title: Cardiorespiratory and Muscular Rehabilitation of Children and Young Adults With Marfan Syndrome.
papers.summary:
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a rare genetic disease (1/5000) characterized by the association of ocular impairment, cardiovascular disease and musculoskeletal disease.

In some chronic conditions, physical activity and training have been shown to be effective in improving muscle strength and functional abilities but also fatigue and quality of life.
